next_step: Deliver SOC 2 / ISO 27001 mapping deck + VPC lab demo; schedule legal for BAA review
notes:
Summary: Silverpine is a mid-stage regtech vendor building a compliance automation product for financial services customers. Primary ask: private VPC deployment with clear compliance mapping across SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA (BAA) and PCI considerations. They want to minimize PCI scope and prove audit logging and KMS-bound key control.

Key constraints / requirements (customer language):
- 'We cannot send PHI out of our VPC without a BAA and dedicated audit pipeline.'
- Data residency: primary tenancy in US (us-east) with EU region for EU customers; need residency guarantees + export controls documented.
- KMS: must integrate with customer-managed AWS KMS/HSM; Redwood must support key usage audit and key rotation policies.
- Audit logging: immutable logs to central SIEM (Splunk) + 7 year retention for compliance use cases.
- Identity: SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning required.
- Security posture proof points: SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certificate, penetration test report, and network design for VPC peering.

Timeline / recent activities (bulleted):
- 2026-01-15: Intro call (Ava Chen) — high level requirements captured; asked for SOC2 evidence and VPC reference architecture.
- 2026-02-02: Technical deep-dive w/ Diego (SE) and infra team — discussed KMS integration patterns (Bring Your Own Key), VPC NAT/egress controls, SIEM forwarding. Fireflies ff_2026-02-18_01 transcript.
- 2026-02-22: Security questionnaire sent (shared drive link). Waiting on Redwood responses to ISO control mapping.
- 2026-03-02: Legal + security call — customer asked for draft BAA language and PCI scope reduction options (tokenization, client-side encryption). Fireflies ff_2026-03-02_02.
- 2026-03-04: Internal follow-up with customer; requested VPC lab demo and SOC2/ISO mapping doc.

POC scope we proposed:
- 2-week VPC lab: dedicated VPC with private endpoints, KMS BYOK flow, audit log forwarding to customer's Splunk instance, sample workload (document redaction + audit report generation).
- Evaluation criteria: ability to demonstrate end-to-end key rotation without data re-encryption, complete audit trail for request->response, latency under 60ms p50 for internal chat workload, and clear evidence of data residency enforcement.

Compliance mapping notes (from SE):
- SOC 2: Redwood SOC 2 artifacts requested; customer needs mapping of Redwood controls to Silverpine control categories (CC1-CC9). Focus on Change Management, Access Controls, Logging & Monitoring.
- ISO 27001: customer expects statement of applicability and a short mapping tying Redwood's runtime controls to A.8/A.12/A.13 controls.
- HIPAA/BAA: will require explicit BAA and confirmation that PHI will not persist outside their VPC unless explicitly configured. Need to document egress paths and any temporary cache behaviors.
- PCI: looking to reduce cardholder data environment (CDE) by pushing tokenization to client-side and ensuring logs do not capture PAN. Need advice from Redwood on PCI scoping for hosted vs private.

Open questions for Redwood product/security:
- Can Redwood provide per-tenant key usage logs (KMS audit) surfaced to customer and retained for X years?
- What is the canonical VPC architecture for Private deployments (peering vs Transit Gateway)? Provide diagram and bandwidth/latency expectations.
- Any controls to guarantee zero-durable-storage of prompts/responses outside customer-managed storage?
- PCI: any prior customers who used Redwood Private to achieve scope reduction?

Next steps agreed:
- Deliver SOC2/ISO mapping deck by 2026-03-12 (owner: Diego).
- Schedule VPC lab demo week of 2026-03-22 (owner: Ava).
- Legal to send draft BAA to Silverpine counsel by 2026-03-15 (owner: Redwood legal liaison).

Sales notes / tone: Broader opportunity across their financial services customers. Very cost-conscious but will pay for compliance guarantees. This is a strategic enterprise deal (target ARR $200k+). Keep communications technical and legal-heavy; involve SE and security early.
